claim_verdicts.evidence: Docs mirror, .NET 10 moniker block (range=">= aspnetcore-10.0"): "WebApplication.CreateBuilder ... initializes a new instance of the WebApplicationBuilder class with preconfigured defaults". The same page shows `var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);` followed by `builder.Services.Add...` and `builder.Configuration`, i.e. services and configuration are registered on that object.

fundamentals/middleware/index.md:55 "The call to WebApplication.Run ... at the end of the code block runs the app and blocks the calling thread until host shutdown." fundamentals/servers/index.md: "Kestrel server is the default, cross-platform HTTP server implementation" (this app self-hosts in a Linux container; no IIS). Ran on SDK 10.0.300: after builder.Build(), builder.Services.AddSingleton<object>() throws InvalidOperationException "The service collection cannot be modified because it is read-only" - registration really does end at Build().

.NET docs mirror: "Service registration is order-independent except when registering multiple implementations of the same type." Every builder.Services.Add... call in Program.cs lines 10-50 registers a distinct type (AddControllers, AddProblemDetails, AddDonHangInfrastructure -> DonHangDbContext/IOrderRepository/INotifier, OrderService, JwtTokenService, AddAuthentication/AddJwtBearer, AddAuthorization, AddCors), so the exception does not apply.

fundamentals/routing.md:73 "An endpoint is something that can be: Selected, by matching the URL and HTTP method. Executed, by running the delegate." mvc/controllers/routing.md:94 "Call MapControllers to map attribute routed controllers." Ran a controller with [Route("api/v1/ping")] + [HttpGet] and [HttpGet("{id:int}")] on dotnet 10.0.300: GET /api/v1/ping -> 200, POST /api/v1/ping -> 405; one method-and-path pair per attribute-routed action.

Local run, dotnet 10.0.300: action body List() contains Console.WriteLine("list ran"); the startup log shows only "startup: MapControllers done", "Now listening on: http://127.0.0.1:5199", "Application started" - no "list ran". After two GET /api/v1/ping the log shows "list ran" exactly twice. The method body runs per matching request, not when MapControllers() executes.

issues.quote: Please move `app.UseAuthentication();` to right after `app.UseCors();` and before `app.UseMiddleware<RequestLoggingMiddleware>();`
issues.text: The scenario's reorder request is impossible against the file the lesson just quoted. In Program.cs lines 67-72 the order is ExceptionHandling, RequestLogging, UseCors, UseAuthentication, UseAuthorization: UseAuthentication is ALREADY immediately after UseCors, and UseCors itself comes after RequestLogging, so "right after UseCors" and "before RequestLoggingMiddleware" cannot both hold. A reader who checks the code can therefore defend option d ("The reviewer's suggested line order is itself wrong"), which makes the key ambiguous.
issues.fix: Rewrite the review comment in `context` as one coherent move, e.g. "Please move `app.UseAuthentication();` above `app.UseMiddleware<RequestLoggingMiddleware>();` - the current order is a bug." Keep answer a; option d's explanation then holds (the scenario really says nothing about whether that move is right).

issues.quote: Everything an ASP.NET Core app needs before it can run — a database connection, a way to prove a customer has signed in, and so on — gets registered on that one object.
issues.text: "Everything" overstates it: the docs say CreateBuilder hands back the builder "with preconfigured defaults" - configuration sources, logging and the server itself are already in place and the app never registers them. What goes on builder.Services is what this app adds on top of those defaults.
issues.fix: Change to: "Whatever this app needs on top of what the framework already sets up - what it uses to reach the database, a way to prove a customer has signed in, and so on - gets registered on that one object."

issues.quote: app.MapControllers(), is the one that creates every **endpoint** this app has
issues.text: Unlisted claim: "the one that creates every endpoint this app has" is a checkable fact about DonHang.Api (MapControllers is the only endpoint-creating call in Program.cs), not a general property of MapControllers, and no claim in the ledger carries it (claim 4 only covers what MapControllers does).
issues.fix: Keep the sentence (true at stage-1: Program.cs lines 64-72 contain no other Map* call) and add a fact claim to .meta.json, section 4: "In DonHang.Api/Program.cs at stage-1, app.MapControllers() is the only endpoint-creating call, so every endpoint the app has comes from it."

issues.quote: register the pieces the app needs to reach the database, a standard error format (`AddProblemDetails()`), an order service, and a way to prove a customer has signed in
issues.text: Two mismatches with the source. AddDonHangInfrastructure registers DonHangDbContext, IOrderRepository AND INotifier/LoggingNotifier - the notifier is not a piece for reaching the database. JwtTokenService's only member is IssueToken(int customerId, string email): it hands out the proof, it does not prove or check anything; the checking is AddAuthentication/AddJwtBearer on line 25, outside the quoted block.
issues.fix: Write: "...register the infrastructure pieces this app runs on (among them everything it uses to reach the database), a standard error format (`AddProblemDetails()`), an order service, and a way to give a signed-in customer something it can show on later requests."

issues.quote: `app.MapControllers()` creates one for every attribute-routed method it finds.
issues.text: True in this app only. An action method may carry several route attributes and each one produces its own endpoint; the routing docs note "All of the HTTP verb attributes accept a route template" and show several templates per action. Each ProductsController method carries exactly one, so the file matches, but the summary states it as a general rule.
issues.fix: Reword summary line 3 to "...`app.MapControllers()` creates one for each route attribute it finds - one per method in `ProductsController`." (or add "in this app").

issues.text: The fill answer set has a single spelling. Comparison is case-insensitive and trimmed (docs/01), but a learner who types the call as the lesson writes it (MapControllers()) or repeats the prefix (app.MapControllers) is marked wrong for no content reason.

The prose lists 'send notifications' among what this block does, but no line is named as the one doing it. I can map 'a standard error format' to `AddProblemDetails()` and 'an order service' to `AddScoped<OrderService>()` because those names appear, yet nothing tells me notifications come out of `AddDonHangInfrastructure(connectionString)` — a call whose name and only argument both point at the database.
issues.fix: In section 5, name the call: replace 'the pieces the app needs to reach the database and send notifications' with 'the pieces the app needs to reach the database and send notifications (`AddDonHangInfrastructure`)'.
issues.quote: The rest read the connection string and register the pieces the app needs to reach the database and send notifications, a standard error format (`AddProblemDetails()`), an order service, and a way to hand out proof that a customer has signed in.
